notes: This review compares deterministic builder output against the prior hand-built enriched examples.
The review is provisional and not human validation.
No runtime integration or model call was performed.

comparison_to_hand_built_examples.generated_strength: The generated brief preserves the key launch-beta signal: the interpretation separates an already-conditional starting direction from a sharpened action consequence around paid private pilots, buyer behavior, and named public-launch outcomes.
comparison_to_hand_built_examples.generated_weakness: The generated section repeats template phrases and some interpreted values, so it feels less humane than the hand-built example.
comparison_to_hand_built_examples.comparison_read: The builder output carries the hand-built intent but should be patched before testing another case.

comparison_to_hand_built_examples.generated_strength: The generated brief preserves the deployment signal: the interpretation distinguishes the earlier narrow-pilot posture from the sharpened consequence of a backlog diagnostic, fewer operating gates, and hard pause triggers.
comparison_to_hand_built_examples.generated_weakness: The generated prose is more mechanical than the hand-built version and repeats phrases such as visible thresholds and visible evidence gates.
comparison_to_hand_built_examples.comparison_read: The builder output is rule-compliant and useful, but the templates need a small language patch before a third builder case.

rule_compliance.rule_compliance_summary: The deterministic builder complied with PR139 rules, but rule compliance alone did not make the output as readable as the hand-built examples.

readability_assessment.readability_summary: The generated outputs are safe and informative, but they read like deterministic scaffolding rather than polished product-facing briefs.

risk_assessment.source_depth_risk: Source depth remains limited because the builder uses checked-in-safe interpretation reads and does not inspect raw/private conversation context.
risk_assessment.overclaim_risk: The builder avoids explicit proof language, but smoother generated prose could still make provisional interpretation feel more settled than it is.
risk_assessment.product_language_risk: The current templates repeat source-derived phrasing and can sound mechanical compared with the hand-built examples.
risk_assessment.quality_label_risk: Useful friction remains described as a non-scoring read, and evidence-only fields stay out of the main body.
risk_assessment.runtime_integration_risk: Runtime integration would be premature because the builder has not yet shown humane enough output or local-private adequacy across builder-generated cases.
risk_assessment.strongest_risk: The strongest risk is product-language drift: deterministic templates can be safe but still too stiff to serve a user-facing brief.

decision_gate.rationale: The builder produced safe, rule-compliant enriched briefs for both existing cases, but the generated language is more repetitive and mechanical than the hand-built examples. A narrow rule/template patch should come before a third builder case.

next_recommendation.recommended_next_pr: PR142 Decision Work Brief Enrichment Builder Rule Patch v0
next_recommendation.recommended_action: Patch the enrichment templates so generated prose is less repetitive while preserving PR139 field limits, uncertainty, source refs, and non-claims.
not_recommended: third builder case before template patch
